old_title: Leicestershire charged by ECB, Nottinghamshire v Hampshire, and more: county cricket, day one - live
new_title: County cricket: title race hots up while Leicestershire charged by ECB - as it happened
old_text:
A fourth wicket at Derby where I imagine Fletch has sighed a long, inextinguisable sigh. Wayne Madsen lbw to Khaled, turned inside out until he was facing the square leg umpire. Derby 74-4.
And I think the rain might be returning to OT. Sharma has whistled out a second at CLS, Rhodes dislodging his own bail by dusting a ball into his own stumps.
Meanwhile talented 17 year old Manny Lumsden is having his first bowl in first-class cricket at Trent Bridge. A lovely action, and he gets through it, Kyle Abbott whispering in his ear from mid off, despite being dispatched for four first ball by Haynes.
Northants have won the toss at New Road and chosen to have a bowl. Their bowling includes Harry Conway in place of fellow Aussie Nathan McSweeney.
Listening in to the excellent BBC coverage from Trent Bridge, where they agree that Leicestershire, if found guilty, will be docked 19 points. Grace Road, meanwhile, "strongly dispute the allegations."
Huge thanks to Mike Birtwhistle in the Lancashire scorebox for some handmade ginger snap biscuits which are both very gingery and make a satisfying snap when you crack them. The rain has stopped, the covers are being unfolded but no news yet on when we will restart.
"Sunshine at Headingley," writes Tim Maitland. "I'm not imagining it. You can clearly see it as they drag the hose around the ground to try and clear off the precipitation."
Meanwhile all-conquering Durham, who need a maxiumum of 17 points to confirm promotion, have lost Ben McKinney for 26, a wicket for young Sharma. Durham 43-1.
The champions are wobbling. From 18-0, Nottinghamshire are suddenly 20-3 against Hampshire. HH, Slater and McCann all back in the pavilion. Two for the evergreen Kyle Abbott. The pitch is an interesting shade of bile.
Middlesex will lose director of cricket Alan Coleman at the end of the season, saying: ""I will leave Middlesex with two senior teams with exceptional young talent and huge potential to achieve success in the game, supported by a dedicated staff who will no doubt continue to guide these players well through the coming seasons" Interim CEO Julie Harrington promised that Middx would build on "his philosophy of wanting to win with homegrown players."
Derbyshire's season seems to be careering to a close. After thrashings by Durham and Gloucestershire, they were 0 for two off two balls against Kent, thanks to the wiley Hasan Mahmud. They've recovered to 17-2.
Bat black skies now above OT. Perhaps suprisingly Gloucestershire have not chosen new young signing Che Simmons for this game. Ben Walkden has dropped Phillips at third slip but Gloucestershire have survived six and a half overs without further collapse.
At Sophia Gardens, Grace Road, Hove, New Road and Headingley, where Yorkshire reached 9-0 before the rain arrived.
The Met Office say things will get better: "Heavy rain slowly clearing the southeast in the morning. A brighter day for many and feeling fresh. Winds gradually easing in the north, with showers too."
Arrive at Old Trafford to bright sunshine if threatening skies, to find Gloucestershire have won the toss, chosen to bat against Jimmy Anderson and are 3-1. Middleton feathered an edge behind off Jimmy's second ball. One change for Lancs, Mitch Stanley in for Tom Bailey.
Notts have signed New Zealand wicketkeeper-batter Mitchell Hay for the last three matches after Kyle Verreynne was recalled by South Africa
Essex are running on empty, without Simon Harmer (recalled by South Africa), Sam Cook and Jordan Cox (England), Charlie Bennett and Noah Thain (injury). They've brought inteenager Jack Auld on a rookie contract.
Warwickshire' Che Simmons has joined Gloucestershire on loan until the end of the season ahead of a permanent move.
Preamble - Leicesteshire charged with breaching ECB pitch regulations
Good morning! There are conkers on the ground now, and even the hardiest marigolds are fading into September. Just three rounds to go, and the chase is still on - for promotion and for the holy grail itself.
Could things finally go Somerset's way? We will know more after their visit to Grace Road, where opponents Leicestershire are in a desperate fight for survival, and it looks as if if their summer is about to get worse. They have been charged with breaching the ECB Pitch Regulations after officials reported their pitch for the match against Glamorgan at the end of August. The matter has been passed to the independent Cricket Discipline Panel for adjudication where they will make the decision "as quickly as appropriately as possible" bearing in mind the ramifications.
We will chew over this, and the other comings and goings, over the next four days. Play starts at 10.30am, do join us.
new_text:
The three leading contenders for the Division One title, Somerset, Warwickshire and Nottinghamshire, each had a profitable day, though Warwickshire swung the biggest hammer after dismissing Glamorgan for 69 at Sophia Gardens.
Ethan Bamber was chief destroyer, with five for 28, passing 50 wickets for the season, while Ed Barnard (three for five) provided able backup. There were no demons in the dirt for the visitors, who eased to 154 for three.
Joe Clarke hit his fourth Championship century of the season to rescue Nottinghamshire from the doldrums of 20 for three as Hampshire's Kyle Abbott made the most of a bile-coloured pitch. Liam Patterson-White (92) and the tail then sailed Notts past 350. Felix Organ and Nick Gubbins survived four overs of evening torment from Olly Stone and Dillon Pennington.
Somerset arrived at Grace Road to find the mood music gloomy after Leicestershire were charged with breaching pitch regulations during their match against Glamorgan in August. Leicestershire "strongly dispute the allegations", but risk losing the 19 points from that game if the Cricket Discipline Panel finds against them, a kick in the teeth to their hopes of staying in Division One.
Spirits will not have been any brighter when Somerset's Josh Thomas and Tom Lammonby added 181 for the first wicket. Thomas, just 21 pocketed his third hundred of the year.
Derbyshire fought back from nought for two after two balls against Kent, thanks to an undefeated 129 from Martin Andersson and 47 extras. Bangladesh pace bowler Hasan Mahmud grabbed four wickets. Promotion chasing Kent had four overs to bat and Ben Compton was inevitably [Ben] Aitchisoned.
George Balderson, three for 35 and a run out, had a good day out against Gloucestershire at Old Trafford; while Essex had the best - just - of a relegation rumble against Yorkshire, who lost five for 18 after a prosperous morning.
Plenty of action between the showers, with good days for all the leading contenders: Somerset, Notts and, above all Warwickshire. We'll be back tomorrow. Thanks for your company - bye!
As I'm watching a handful of groundstaff crouch around the OT covers and stare at the radar on their phones, I'd better write up. Do keep chatting BTL as Notts, Somerset and Warwicks battle for supremacy.
What a pick 21 year old Josh Thomas has been at the top of the order for Somerset. He celelebrates century number three of the season, matching James Haynes, and teammates Craig Overton and Tom Abell. Only two men have more in Division One: Dan Lawrence (5), and Joe Clarke (4).
He doesn't last much longer, b White for 100. Somerset 222-3
The commentators are just pondering whether this could be the last ball of Anderson's spell when Hammond chances a quick single to mid-on where Balderson picks up and hits. Oh dear. Glos 121-6.
And here comes Noman Ali for his first bowl of the day.
As the skies darken again at OT, Anderson frowns upon Gloucestershire, Dhariwal caught behind for 20. Gloucs 106-5. The umpires take a look at their light meters.
Derbyshire and Durham's fortunes are mirroring each other today - Durham are 196-9 against Middlesex, with Parkinson and Raine adding a so-far-un-broken 32 for the last wicket. And Derbyshire 197-7 against Middx, thanks to an unbeaten 71 from Andersson.
Tom Lammonby will be fuming about that lapse of concentration, caught on the boundary for 74 having been largely untroubled all day. Green the bowler. Somerset 181-1.
A quick walk around Old Trafford at tea, it is very autumnal out there and was definitely a mistake to wear sandals. There's been a double bowling change, Anderson retakes the ball at his own end and the impressive Ben Walkden has his first over of the day from the Brian Statham end.
They take tea at Sophia Gardens where Somerset will munch happily, Lammonby and Thomas racing along at over five an over. Fellow Championship chasers Warwickshire have Glamorgan 61-9, while Joe Clarke, with his fourth century in the season, has taken Notts to a not-quite-but-almost-comfortable 249-6.
Hands in pockets for the Lancashire slips, as Stanley bundles in. Gloucestershire 74-4 - I think I missed two-centuries Bracey getting out, nibbling behind, a third for Balderson for 21.
Shame about the washout at Hove, today was the "wear yellow" celebration of the 200th birthday of John Wisden, born on September 5 1826. I hope a CCLive reader got one of those nice anniversary umbrellas they were giving away to early arrivals.
In Division Two, they are playing hokey-cokey with the covers at Old Trafford, with the sun currently out but the hover cover defiantly on - Gloucs 58-3.
Derbyshire have recovered thanks to a defiant fifty from Martin Andersson, 155-5 against Kent; Middlesex's Morgan and Sharma, who bowled so well against Lancs here early season, now have Durham in trouble at 146-6; while Libby (50) and Hose have moved Worcesteshire along to a more comfortable 89-2 against Northants.
Right, head back above water, to discover Glamorgan have collapsed, again - 48 for six against Warwickshire; Somerset are flying against Leicestershire - 124-0; Joe Clarke (86) has saved Notts' blushes, 202-4; and Yorkshire are plodding along, 129-2, Lyth unbeaten on 61.
Bustling Balderson does it again, bowling Phillips for eight, Gloucestershire 44-2. Ken, watching with keener eyes than me thinks it may have kept down a little, anyhow, it zipped through the gate without any manners.
They've just started at New Road (the inevitable Ben Sanderson dismissing Lategan for 0), Worcs 10-1; and they'll keep playing at Headingley until 12.50, where Lyth and Luxton have so far kept out Porter and Snater, Lancashire's George Bell behind the stumps after signing on a short-term loan.
